structure: CSharp native constructor/status-out/ref argument and handle drop code compared to Native native_handles, call argument/result and startup binding paths. Semantic handle is affine, CSharp represents its one word in an ABI struct and Native uses pointer values; readonly reference passes the handle word address to the C shim.
branches: Dynamic library load and declared drop-symbol resolution occur before calls, with non-null checks. Direct constructor result is non-null; status0 loads and validates the out value, nonzero builds Err without validating an absent output. Scope and early return must drop each successful handle exactly once; an Err does not drop an owner.
logic: Fixture follows existing tests/cpp-interop/handle_fixture.cpp CounterHandle struct ABI: create returns one word, methods take const CounterHandle*, destructor takes the raw word. Original preliminary raw-pointer method fixture was the wrong C-side ABI and is retained as preparation evidence, not a compiler defect.
diagnostics: CSharp3 passes normal return, early return/control, and success/error status-out result paths. No CSharp production source change warranted. Native focused proof must match actual values and destructor counts; no whole Native.cs or target/platform closure.
rootCause: CSharp BuildTypeDefinitions registers every parsed struct, including native/COM affine handles, before enums and named boxes. Native reference registerCurrent excludes affine declarations and only seeds kind1; registerNamedBoxes correctly includes affine kind9, so its catalog count differs and metadata signature registration returns InvalidSource. Diagnostic91 independently reports function-emission SignatureRegistration and type-universe capture failure.
fix: Include affine nominal declarations using the existing alias-qualified name helper and seed kind9 through the same named identity map as ordinary kind1 nominals. Keep CSharp struct-before-enum/box ordering, complete catalogs, cache validation and diagnostics; no cache disabling or synthesized fallback identity.
